title: Runway microplateau credit & HC allocation probe
body:
Executive summary:
We ran a rapid probe to understand how a small, staged credit pool ("microplateau") plus a targeted headcount reallocation would affect runway and SLA coverage under three demand/price outcomes. This is a working sheet for discussion with product and engineering leadership — not final financials.

Key idea: microplateau credit pool
- Create a 3-month, $750k encoded credit bucket that can be deployed to high-velocity customers for short windows (4–8 weeks) to blunt attrition when demand spikes or price experiments degrade take-rate.
- Credits are drawn down before invoking permanent pricing changes or HC adjustments. Credits expire if unused.
- Expected effect: reduces immediate churn, buys time to flip slab or adjust model mix.

Scenarios (simplified):
- Base (current run-rate): monthly revenue $12.5M, gross margin 38%, burn rate (op ex + infra) $10.2M/month, runway 15 months (post-credit).
- Microshock (20% drop in take-rate from price test / competitor move): revenue -20% over 12 weeks unless mitigated.
- Growth (20% higher take-rate from new enterprise win + higher embed demand): revenue +20% sustained.

Assumptions and lever effects (one-pagers):
- Pricing levers: small per-token uplift (1–3%), targeted slab discounts, and time-bound credits.
- HC levers: hiring pause for non-critical roles, 10% contractor conversion, 6-week delay on new SRE hires.
- Cost levers: aggressive infra quantization plan (projected 8–12% infra savings by Q4), delayed non-essential OSS spend.

Summary table (monthly impact, approximate):
Scenario | Rev ($M/mo) | GM% | Net burn ($M/mo) | Runway (months)
Base | 12.5 | 38 | 10.2 | 15
Microshock (no mitigation) | 10.0 | 36 | 11.8 | 12
Microshock + microplateau credits + HC tilt | 10.8 | 37 | 10.9 | 14
Growth (no spend change) | 15.0 | 40 | 9.1 | 19

Headcount reallocation (targeted, 6-month phasing):
- Reassign 4 PMs from speculative platform work to enterprise onboarding (reduces hiring need by 2 FTE in sales ops).
- Freeze 3 junior backend roles (hiring deferred 12 weeks).
- Convert 6 contractor inference engineers to 4 FTEs where retention is high (net FTE change -2, saves ~12% on contractor premium).
- SRE: delay 2 hires, but fund 1 critical on-call rotation uplift to avoid SLA risk.

Pricing sensitivity slice (illustrative):
- Per-token +2% across main model family -> estimated revenue lift +3.0% (elasticity calibrated to recent A/B tests). Churn risk minimal for mid-tier customers, higher for low-touch.
- Slab discount expansion (larger slabs at lower unit price) increases committed volume but reduces blended rev per token by ~4% at full uptake; breakeven occurs if committed volume increases >25%.
- Time-bound credits reduce immediate churn by ~6–9% in cohorts receiving credits (pilot projection).

Trigger rules for drawing microplateau credits:
- Activation if MRR drop in top-10 customers >5% week-over-week for two consecutive weeks AND retention delta forecast >$250k ARR churn risk.
- Max two activations per customer per 12 months.
- Finance approval required for activations >$50k.

Monitoring and instrumentation needed:
- Cohort-level churn delta dashboard (daily feed).
- Per-customer cost-to-serve (tokens, quantization mix) and SLA impact.
- Fast experiment channel between product (pricing), sales (contracts), and finance for near-real-time decisions.

Risks and unknowns:
- Credits can mask deeper product issues leading to repeated use; need strict expiration and post-activation review playbook.
- Elasticity estimates are noisy for enterprise-segment; require 6–8 week A/B rolling windows.
- Operational complexity: administering many small credits adds bookkeeping overhead — propose automation pipeline up-front.

Next steps (owner: Aisha):
1) Run a 6-week micropilot with 5 customers (mixed mid-enterprise and scale-ups) to validate churn lift and reconciliation overhead. Deadline: 2026-09-01.
2) Produce a 12-week HC re-phasing plan with engineering leads that maps role-by-role delay/convert options. Draft due: 2026-07-23.
3) Wire up a daily dashboard for top-100 customers with churn risk signal and cost-to-serve by 2026-08-15 (paired with analytics).
4) Legal to draft standard microcredit terms (expiration, non-transfer) by 2026-07-30.

Notes / open questions (working):
- How to account for credits in GAAP revenue recognition for short windows? (Finance/Legal follow-up).
- If credits are used repeatedly for same customer, propose escalation path to Sales + CSM for product fixes.
- Consider combining credits with auto-quantization profile activation to reduce cost-to-serve for the cohort concurrently.

Appendix: quick sensitivity grid (runway months vs. blended rev change)
- -6% blended rev -> runway -2.5 months
- -3% blended rev -> runway -1.2 months
- +3% blended rev -> runway +1.8 months

Contact: Aisha Patel (aisha.patel@redwood.com) — comments inline preferred.

This file is a working sheet: keep change log in comments; move to "final" only after pilot outcomes and legal sign-off.
